blocks.html_en:
> A world where business and communication is conducted primarily online cannot coexist with low cost, widely distributed, undetectable identity theft.

what if we dont use centralized identity at all?

web of trust failed in the 90s because exchanging keys is hard when all you have is desktop computers, wired connections and old school hackers who dont care about ux. today you could set up a system where the whole process is tap two phones together with nfc and confirm, everything gets auto downloaded and shared with your whole network.

now this doesnt work directly for a random online business where none of your contact personally know anyone, but governments can act as an authority that cross signs their citizens keys. that means if you want to stop bots from creating accounts all you have to do is make new users show a certificate from one of the authorities you trust.

its cheap to verify, decentralized and not hard to integrate with existing PKI. the biggest technical problem is key management as always, but that can be solved with something like ethereum style social recovery setups or a did:plc type multi key scheme.

that gives you a robust identity scheme. browsers and social media can integrate it to show a trust rating for content based on who signed it. messaging apps can show a warning or refuse calls from unknown users. fraud is only possible against a person who somehow has no irl contacts, never used a government service in their life and trusts random strangers online. at that point they deserve it.

the one massive, unpredictable question is if anybody is willing to go ahead and adopt it on a scale big enough to create network effects. it would take a state level force and carefully designed OS integrations so its more convenient than email/password signup.

but even if all of this fails i still think a world of scams is better than a world controlled by a couple big countries (America, China, maybe EU) or for-profit corporations. open source ai might lead to anarchy but closed ai will definitely get us to tyranny. i dont know about you but i would take the first option.

sentences.zh: 今天，您可以建立一个系统，整个过程只需用 NFC 轻触两部手机并确认，所有内容都会自动下载并与您的整个网络共享。现在，这不适用于随机在线业务，您的联系人都不认识任何人，但政府可以充当交叉签署其公民密钥的权威机构。

sentences.zh: 最大的技术问题一如既往地是密钥管理，但这可以通过以太坊风格的社交恢复设置或 did:plc 类型的多密钥方案来解决。这为您提供了一个强大的身份方案。

sentences.en: browsers and social media can integrate it to show a trust rating for content based on who signed it.
sentences.zh: 浏览器和社交媒体可以将其集成，以根据签名者显示内容的信任评级。

sentences.en: messaging apps can show a warning or refuse calls from unknown users.

sentences.en: at that point they deserve it.the one massive, unpredictable question is if anybody is willing to go ahead and adopt it on a scale big enough to create network effects.
sentences.zh: 到那时他们就应该得到它。一个巨大的、不可预测的问题是，是否有人愿意继续并大规模采用它以产生网络效应。

blocks.html_en: It’s a long term pattern. When you’re winning (Anthropic), you keep the tech closed and try to monetize it as much as possible. When you’re losing (Meta), you open it up or drag it into a standards committee to either devalue it or slow the leader down while you prepare a “standard” version of it. You also highlight how altruistic and morally good you are for having done so. There is nothing new under the sun. It’s all a game.

sentences.en: It’s a long term pattern.
sentences.zh: 这是一个长期的模式。

sentences.en: When you’re winning (Anthropic), you keep the tech closed and try to monetize it as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 当你获胜时（人择），你会保持技术封闭并尝试尽可能地将其货币化。

sentences.en: When you’re losing (Meta), you open it up or drag it into a standards committee to either devalue it or slow the leader down while you prepare a “standard” version of it.
sentences.zh: 当你失去（元）时，你可以将其打开或拖入标准委员会，以使其贬值或在准备其“标准”版本时减慢领导者的速度。

sentences.en: You also highlight how altruistic and morally good you are for having done so.
sentences.zh: 您还强调了您这样做是多么无私和道德上的善良。

sentences.en: There is nothing new under the sun.
sentences.zh: 太阳底下并无新事。

sentences.en: It’s all a game.
sentences.zh: 这都是一场游戏。

blocks.html_en:
The governing body is only the western allies. USA + AUS + EU. Or anyone else that may sign a deeply disturbing and restrictive treaty. It's to make sure that the global majority does not make a better model or have access to the same hardware. As is currently the case with embargoes on EUV machines going to China, etc.

Models are not a moat, and I think OpenAI/Anthropic know this. They know that their IPO is being weakened by the open models. Neither is hardware. We are not far from other countries catching up with silicon that matches or exceeds western capabilities, and it will be cheaper.

sentences.en: The governing body is only the western allies.
sentences.zh: 管理机构只有西方盟友。

sentences.en: USA + AUS + EU.
sentences.zh: 美国+澳大利亚+欧盟。

sentences.en: Or anyone else that may sign a deeply disturbing and restrictive treaty.
sentences.zh: 或者任何其他可能签署令人深感不安和限制性条约的人。

sentences.en: It's to make sure that the global majority does not make a better model or have access to the same hardware.
sentences.zh: 这是为了确保全球大多数人不会制造出更好的模型或无法使用相同的硬件。

sentences.en: As is currently the case with embargoes on EUV machines going to China, etc.Models are not a moat, and I think OpenAI/Anthropic know this.
sentences.zh: 就像目前对进入中国的 EUV 机器实施禁运等情况一样。模型不是护城河，我认为 OpenAI/Anthropic 知道这一点。

sentences.en: They know that their IPO is being weakened by the open models.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，开放模式正在削弱他们的首次公开募股。

sentences.en: Neither is hardware.
sentences.zh: 硬件也不是。

sentences.en: We are not far from other countries catching up with silicon that matches or exceeds western capabilities, and it will be cheaper.
sentences.zh: 我们离其他国家赶上与西方能力相当或超过西方能力的硅不远了，而且它会更便宜。

blocks.html_en:
> The crew are saying that the request came in on a frequency they weren't monitoring

There is only one channel you are supposed to monitor, it’s 16. That’s also where the coast guards make all their announcement/requests for help and whatnot. The reason there is a single channel to monitor is precisely to avoid the situation of different vessels being on standby on different frequencies and thus being unable to hear each others.

So that means they weren’t monitoring 16. Which is unacceptable.

I know I need to have 16 on at all times, and i am not a professional super yacht captain.

blocks.html_en:
On the sea there are 2 levels of distress. Things are going wrong and may end up in a mayday call (pan pan) and things have gone wrong human life is in imminent danger.

I have no doubt that a boat without propulsion is a pan pan call.

When traveling the seas a watch must be maintained at all times using all available means. This involes looking, listening, and the use of any electronics available. The most common electronic device on a boat is probably a VHF radio. Channel 16 is the channel to monitor on watch. Well equipped boats will have multiple VHF radios to monitor more then one channel.

I have no doubt the boat was well equipped with a professional captain. The other professional Captain in this story made a stink because launchpad was the closest vessel and they ignored a very old fundamental rule of the sea.

This story has a happy ending because another vessel stepped up. We don’t know the alternative.

The Captain of the Launchpad is choosing the inability to keep a vhf radio set to channel 16 rather than admit they ignored the call.

When traveling the seas a watch must be maintained at all times using all available means. This involes looking, listening, and the use of any electronics available. The most common electronic device on a boat is probably a VHF radio. Channel 16 is the channel to monitor on watch. Well equipped boats will have multiple VHF radios to monitor more then one channel.

I have no doubt the boat was well equipped with a professional captain. The other professional Captain in this story made a stink because launchpad was the closest vessel and they ignored a very old fundamental rule of the sea.

This story has a happy ending because another vessel stepped up. We don’t know the alternative.

The Captain of the Launchpad is choosing the inability to keep a vhf radio set to channel 16 rather than admit they ignored the call.

blocks.html_en:
The vessel was at least 100 miles from shore, the USCG did in fact label it a non-emergency. This is "radio shore for your buddy to zoom out with 50 gallons of diesel in a zodiac" territory. CHP doesn't send out an ambulance or medevac helicopter if your car runs out of gas on the side of the road. You get an uber to the gas station, or call your buddy to deliver some gas to you.

The ocean currents in the gulf of alaska aren't particularly strong, you are looking at 1-3 days before getting within sight of land. Similarly, boats are not airplanes, as the philosopher Mitch Hedburg once pointed out, escalators aren't out of order, they are simply stairs. Boats continue to float with or without fuel.

blocks.html_en:
All the Launchpad had to do was respond on the radio to the skiff, the cruise ship, or the USCG. They weren’t obligated to do more.

A pan pan is a non emergency in a deteriorating situation.

I don't know the area or the details at what happend.

There is this quote from the USCG.

“At approximately 9:56 p.m., the Coast Guard determined they [the skiff] were not in distress and issued a marine assistance request broadcast on their behalf,”

Exactly what a pan pan call is.

The biggest issue is the lack of communication and the excuse that a superyacht wasn't monitoring channel 16.

In a democracy there should not be singular parasites that distort democracy by bribes; right now this is clearly the case with a (rather stupid) billionaire controlling the USA but it is a systemic problem.

blocks.html_en:
If you believe, as an increasing number of folks do, that LLMs are basically commoditized at this point or will be soon then there really isn’t a path forward for non open models.

There simply isn’t any value in the models and only in the compute to run them and potentially some higher-order coordination layers.

That’s very bad for the big model labs that banked their future on the opposite, but there just doesn’t seem to be a viable path forward on that approach anymore.

Meta hasn’t been the best global citizen for most of its life, but there may be some mild redemption if it becomes a source of strong open models.

sentences.en: If you believe, as an increasing number of folks do, that LLMs are basically commoditized at this point or will be soon then there really isn’t a path forward for non open models.There simply isn’t any value in the models and only in the compute to run them and potentially some higher-order coordination layers.That’s very bad for the big model labs that banked their future on the opposite, but there just doesn’t seem to be a viable path forward on that approach anymore.Meta hasn’t been the best global citizen for most of its life, but there may be some mild redemption if it becomes a source of strong open models.
sentences.zh: 如果你像越来越多的人那样相信 LLM 基本上已经商品化，或者很快就会商品化，那么非开放模型确实没有前进的道路。模型根本没有任何价值，只有运行它们的计算以及潜在的一些高阶协调层。这对于那些将未来寄托在相反方向的大型模型实验室来说非常糟糕，但在这种方法上似乎不再有可行的前进道路。Meta 还不是最好的全球公民在其生命的大部分时间里，但如果它成为强大的开放模型的来源，可能会有一些温和的救赎。

blocks.html_en:
I strongly prefer a world where open models "win," that said...

I don't understand how we will sustain an ecosystem of open models like the one that exists today. My thoughts go down this path every time I try to put the pieces together:

- Many open models depend on high quality frontier models as a distillation input

- US closed frontier models drive China's open model strategy despite the business model for open models being somewhat fuzzy

- What is the business model that benefits from open weights, exactly? How do their vendors recoup infrastructure and training costs?

I would be grateful to be enlightened on this topic.

The relevant paragraph about Meta’s commitment to open source is here, and the statement is significantly less confident than news is reporting

> • Open source is a positive and important force for empowering people and preventing centralization that is detrimental for both safety and the economy. Meta continues to be strongly supportive of open source, including open source AI models. The current open source ecosystem is strong, and we think it would be a mistake to restrict it. Now that Meta Superintelligence Labs are up and running, we will resume releasing some open source models soon.

“We will resume releasing some open source models soon”??? That’s basically the most ambiguous non commitment ever. Even before legal team watering it down I can’t imagine what the intent is here. We are also going to release open models for things maybe or maybe not kinda? Absolutely zero conviction. And moreover, this explicitly frames the open source ecosystem as something Meta is not a part of.

I have to ask, is this "returns to open models" even correct, considering from a quick look the facebook huggingface collections[0] has been actively releasing different kind of models almost monthly for long time now, possibly even some actual open source ones (looks like Sam 3D had a dataset collection, but didnt look more into it).

Maybe they are not as noteworthy as the recent release, maybe they are too niche for general audience, but its not like they just stopped releasing open weight things and this is their big return, unless i am missing something?

[0]: https://huggingface.co/facebook/collections

My comment was trying to point on the inanity of calling out "so many em-dashes" on a post where it doesn't seem that obvious it was LLM generated. I added some of my own inanity with my remark about them being double-dashes, even though some people undoubtedly find-and-replace the em-dashes in their LLM-generated content something else to try and make it appear more authentic.

But perhaps the best approach would have been to down-vote and move on.

blocks.html_en:
There is no requirement to own the hardware. Even if you own your servers and GPUs - you would not own the power plant, real estate, or internet infrastructure to support it.

It's trivial to rent all of the above components in a competitive market under different periods, you may simply rent the token output from someone who put in the effort on this as well.

An open frontier model induces margin compression on training and inference prices across the industry.

blocks.html_en:
I get that argument, but I don't think it is that bad. Open weights that are out of reach for local use are still within reach for groups of people or small to medium companies. Even if you only rent enough cloud GPUs to run the weights for a few hours, you still get to do anything you want with it.

Worst case you can still archive the weights and hope for capable hardware to get affordable. At the same time this archive is the base line for a new frontier lab to start over if required. I see open weights as a pure upside even though I can't run the bigger models in my home lab.

Worst case you can still archive the weights and hope for capable hardware to get affordable. At the same time this archive is the base line for a new frontier lab to start over if required. I see open weights as a pure upside even though I can't run the bigger models in my home lab.

There's something to be said for making these technologies equitable to those with less resources, but that's due to the cost of hardware and the nature of how transformer models scale... not really anything to do with "open"ness.

blocks.html_en:
This paragraph is wild.

> As a thought experiment, imagine only one person had a superintelligent lawyer. They would have an unfair advantage in court -- even if they were wrong on the merits. That would lead to a worse society. But now imagine everyone has a superintelligent lawyer. In this case, justice would be carried out much more fairly and efficiently than it is today when there is often an imbalance in skills and resources in litigation.

This would only be true in a vacuum. Ignoring several leaps of progress where it would suddenly be allowed for an AI to represent one in court (imagine the size of the context window) and you could also call it from prison. That is not what is imbalanced about the US court system. Whoever has more money can drown someone in court filings and court fees and then drop their case financially ruining someone.

It's also funny how the interest of "AI for everyone" only extends to the national interest but I guess he's got to make sure he stays in good graces with the current administration.

blocks.html_en:
I prefer open models. But in his essay, Zuckerberg's broader picture of the future is not one I want to embrace: everyone with a personal agent that has information on and involvement with every aspect of our lives, including our relationships and hobbies. Like, his daughter loves to bake, so his AI agent chooses recipes and orders ingredients - as if though those aren't enjoyable and meaningful parts of cooking.

Another example Zuckerberg gives is an LLM analyzing his sleep patterns. Do you need an AI to tell you if you're fucking exhausted every day? Is that analysis somehow going to give you more time to sleep?

It's a technocratic fairy tale founded on the idea that modern problems are driven by a lack of personal analysis rather than external pressures that are often systemic and out of our control. So far, LLMs have made a lot of those systemic issues worse: concentrating more wealth in a smaller number of people's hands, increasing consumer electricity and electronic prices, etc.

sentences.en: I prefer open models.
sentences.zh: 我更喜欢开放式模型。

i was wondering why meta has such a hard time with llm development

its the organisational goal of that endeavour

they are doing it in a phase of firing people

so the goal of llm at meta is "to make people redundant" and no matter of HR/PR speak can change it

antrophic and openai have the goal "lets create the future"

whomever they hire and no matter how much money they spend on it, the goal alone will create very different outcomes.

blocks.html_en:
Here’s a personal story from back when I was at Meta that should tell you everything you need to know about how things get built and shipped there.

I was working on a service that was a bit of a disaster. Terrible reliability, performance issues, needlessly complex and brittle code, outages all the time. And this was something that everyone using Facebook or IG directly interacts with. My first couple months were spent desperately trying to get it back in order.

Once when I was in the middle of a SEV-1 my manager set up a meeting and said “you have been doing great work on the operational side, but we already have enough to put in that bucket on your PSC. Stop working on this for the rest of the half and ship one of <useless projects> instead, otherwise I won’t be able to save you in the next review.”

I realized then that I had wrongly thought the team was collectively responsible for ensuring a good user experience, when really everyone at the company is individually responsible for ensuring their own success.

sentences.en: Here’s a personal story from back when I was at Meta that should tell you everything you need to know about how things get built and shipped there.I was working on a service that was a bit of a disaster.
sentences.zh: 这是我在 Meta 时的一个个人故事，它应该告诉你所有你需要知道的关于东西如何构建和交付的信息。我正在开发一项有点灾难的服务。

sentences.en: Terrible reliability, performance issues, needlessly complex and brittle code, outages all the time.
sentences.zh: 糟糕的可靠性、性能问题、不必要的复杂和脆弱的代码、总是中断。

sentences.en: And this was something that everyone using Facebook or IG directly interacts with.
sentences.zh: 这是每个使用 Facebook 或 IG 的人都可以直接互动的东西。

sentences.en: My first couple months were spent desperately trying to get it back in order.Once when I was in the middle of a SEV-1 my manager set up a meeting and said “you have been doing great work on the operational side, but we already have enough to put in that bucket on your PSC.
sentences.zh: 我的前几个月拼命地试图让它恢复正常。有一次，当我在 SEV-1 期间，我的经理召开了一次会议，并说：“你们在运营方面做得很好，但我们已经有足够的资源来投入你们的 PSC 了。

sentences.en: Stop working on this for the rest of the half and ship one of <useless projects> instead, otherwise I won’t be able to save you in the next review.”I realized then that I had wrongly thought the team was collectively responsible for ensuring a good user experience, when really everyone at the company is individually responsible for ensuring their own success.
sentences.zh: 在剩下的一半时间里停止处理这个问题，而是交付一个<无用的项目>，否则我将无法在下一次审核中拯救你。”然后我意识到，我错误地认为团队集体负责确保良好的用户体验，而实际上公司的每个人都单独负责确保自己的成功。

Your story is an extremely typical one. It's even worse at older tech companies like Google, Oracle, Amazon, Microsoft, and IBM.

Yet these companies are doing well by any standard. Sure, IBM is bad but it's still a $100B company.

Who is even doing useful projects at these companies? Every story I've heard is everyone is doing useless projects for promotions.

Maybe I just don't know how large companies work.

blocks.html_en:
Meta's problem is not models but doing something productive with them. Meta never really nailed that. Just like Google is struggling with this. And MS. It's the classic disruptors dilemma. In order to embrace the new thing, they have to let go of the old thing that has made them rich.

If you look beyond the somewhat tone deaf leadership, the somewhat stale business model of social media, etc. Meta doesn't actually have a whole lot to bring to the table. They probably managed to hire/keep some AI talent with the help of large salaries. But they are knee deep into having made big figure commitments to data center capacity with nothing to show for it yet. Their AI effort is increasingly looking like a repeat of their failed metaverse strategy. A lot of expensive bets that are not paying off.

It all boils down to Mark Zuckerberg not being the visionary and innovator he thinks he is. Like many billionaires he confuses him lucking out in his twenties with some magical leadership qualities or brain capacity he has. And the reality of course is that he lucked into building a nice social networking thingy not hindered by too much technical skill or deep scientific knowledge. Granted, he did that well. But that's 20 years ago. And then he added to that with some strategic acquisitions of stuff that others did (Whatsapp, Instagram, etc) that you might label as spectacularly good acquisitions for Meta.

But he's not going to reinvent AI. He's way out of his depth there. A bit of a technical lightweight without much academic credentials or much of a vision. His "vision" here is copying what the Chinese and others are already doing well. What's lacking is a vision as to how his version of that is going to be any better and win over all those users. Or indeed a vision as to what people are going to do with all this AI. Apparently there is no vision for that in the context of Meta's own products. This is a company going through the motions of being an AI company without any vision whatsoever as to why they are doing that other than a fear of missing out.

sentences.zh: 像许多亿万富翁一样，他将自己二十多岁的幸运与他拥有的一些神奇的领导才能或大脑能力混为一谈。

sentences.en: And the reality of course is that he lucked into building a nice social networking thingy not hindered by too much technical skill or deep scientific knowledge.
sentences.zh: 当然，现实是，他很幸运地建立了一个不错的社交网络，而不受过多的技术技能或深厚的科学知识的阻碍。

sentences.en: Granted, he did that well.
sentences.zh: 当然，他做得很好。

sentences.en: But that's 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 但那是20年前的事了。

sentences.en: And then he added to that with some strategic acquisitions of stuff that others did (Whatsapp, Instagram, etc) that you might label as spectacularly good acquisitions for Meta.
sentences.zh: 然后他补充说，对其他人所做的一些战略收购（Whatsapp、Instagram 等）你可能会认为 Meta 的收购非常好。

blocks.html_en: But he's not going to reinvent AI. He's way out of his depth there. A bit of a technical lightweight without much academic credentials or much of a vision. His "vision" here is copying what the Chinese and others are already doing well. What's lacking is a vision as to how his version of that is going to be any better and win over all those users. Or indeed a vision as to what people are going to do with all this AI. Apparently there is no vision for that in the context of Meta's own products. This is a company going through the motions of being an AI company without any vision whatsoever as to why they are doing that other than a fear of missing out.

blocks.html_en:
From Zuck's own words "we will resume releasing some open source models soon" Why did you pause releasing them in the first place? Why release only some?

Pushes for export controls on China who have released open weights on much more powerful models than Meta (and I believe that trend's not changing any time soon). I guess open models are bad if they're communist.

The entire essay has not one mention of the Metaverse, that little thing they spent $80b on and rebranded the whole company around.

As usual, the only centralised power Zuck hates is one that isn't in his own hands.

blocks.html_en:
Not sure why you’re talking about it doing literally everything for you. I’m sure you can imagine a scenario where it handles annoying things for you and leaves you free to do things you enjoy instead.

Maybe it gets 10 car insurance quotes for you based on 4 models of car you’re considering.

Or figures out which psychologists in some travel distance of you actually take your insurance, are taking new patients, and what availability they have.

I can think of a ton of scenarios where a capable and reliable AI agent could make my life simpler.

blocks.html_en:
Still say Matrix 3 would have been better if the cliffhanger at the end of 2 had been that "the real world" was just another nested layer of the Matrix for those who rejected the primary fiction.

I mean, why bother sending an army like that when one tiny robot could carry in a plague? Or, as demonstrated by Smith, when an Agent can virally infect and take over someone's mind while they're connected?

Even in 1, Smith talked about the first Matrix failing as the humans rejected the paradise they were given, so it would've fitted perfectly into the cannon that minds who reject "the peak of your civilisation" got themselves a dystopia.

sentences.zh: 仍然要说，如果《黑客帝国 2》结尾处的悬念是“现实世界”只是《黑客帝国》的另一层嵌套，对于那些拒绝原著小说的人来说，《黑客帝国 3》会更好。我的意思是，当一个微型机器人可以携带瘟疫时，为什么还要派遣这样的军队呢？

blocks.html_en:
I think that would work better in The Animatrix; putting it in 3 would be a tonal shift, plus a sudden human victory would feel a bit Mary Sue or Deus Ex (ironically) Machina to me.

But in The Animatrix, you could get away with that, plus we can see the early attempts at utopia that Smith described. Perhaps something about how utopia for some people didn't work for others could be illustrated with an auto-antonym on some load-bearing part of the dystopic-utopia?:

  Some believed we lacked the programming language to describe your perfect world.

We can see this even in current discussions of fiction, where people look at e.g. The Culture and see a dystopia, while famously many of the powerful in tech are parodied for taking the wrong lessons from fiction with "At long last, we have created the Torment Nexus from classic sci-fi novel Don't Create The Torment Nexus".

blocks.html_en:
Psalm 135:15-18 is my favorite version of it, the most clear-headed. It reads more as a warning "if you do this, then this will happen" than an unreasonable commandment.

The idols of the nations are silver and gold, made by human hands. They have mouths, but cannot speak, eyes, but cannot see. They have ears, but cannot hear, nor is there breath in their mouths. Those who make them will be like them, and so will all who trust in them.

Don't worry about the scriptures though. It's likely to be just some old thinker pointing out the dangers of technologies of his time. No reason to believe those dangers carry over to today's technologies, probably.

blocks.html_en:
Your bible is truly full of wise words to live by. Not at all the insane ramblings of hallucinating conmen:

1 Kings 18:36-40

36 At the time of sacrifice, the prophet Elijah stepped forward and prayed: “Lord, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel and that I am your servant and have done all these things at your command. 37 Answer me, Lord, answer me, so these people will know that you, Lord, are God, and that you are turning their hearts back again.”

38 Then the fire of the Lord fell and burned up the sacrifice, the wood, the stones and the soil, and also licked up the water in the trench.

39 When all the people saw this, they fell prostrate and cried, “The Lord—he is God! The Lord—he is God!”

40 Then Elijah commanded them, “Seize the prophets of Baal. Don’t let anyone get away!” They seized them, and Elijah had them brought down to the Kishon Valley and slaughtered there.

1 Samuel 18:25-27

25 Saul replied, “Say to David, ‘The king wants no other price for the bride than a hundred Philistine foreskins, to take revenge on his enemies.’” Saul’s plan was to have David fall by the hands of the Philistines.

26 When the attendants told David these things, he was pleased to become the king’s son-in-law. So before the allotted time elapsed, 27 David took his men with him and went out and killed two hundred Philistines and brought back their foreskins. They counted out the full number to the king so that David might become the king’s son-in-law. Then Saul gave him his daughter Michal in marriage.

sentences.zh: 你的圣经确实充满了生活中的智慧话语。

content_html_zh: 我认为 Meta 所做的还不够多，尽管有意在 2023 年通过 llama 的发布拉开了开源竞赛的序幕。总的来说，我不是 Meta 的忠实粉丝，但他们已经做得足够好了，而且也可能是故意的。 我不知道，我不在房间里，我认为值得给他们一些合理的怀疑。没有人是纯粹的好人，也没有人是纯粹的邪恶。 无论如何，这都是净利。免责声明，我在 Deepmind 从事 Gemma 和开放模型的工作，这里的观点是我自己的。EleutherAI (GPT-Neo)、Google Brain (T5X、Bert) 和 HuggingFace 都有开放模型，而 HuggingFace 则在 2023 年和大型 Chatgpt 之前推广开放模型（以及其他人在做开放工作，我没有在这里列出） https://github.com/EleutherAI/gpt-neo/releases https://github.com/google-research/bert https://github.com/google-research/t5x如果您正在学习人工智能模型，那么仍然值得回顾这些模型和代码库，因为它们仍然是当今所产生的技术的基础！ 它会让您对事物的变化有一个很好的了解，就像在使用现代喷气发动机之前学习螺旋桨飞机一样。谷歌在为当前模型奠定框架方面做了很多工作（目前正在与 Gemma 合作）。 但在ChatGPT起飞后，我认为在meta发布其模型之前谷歌不会继续免费发布任何大模型（也许是因为谷歌当时根本没有任何模型）老实说，我认为 T5 模型系列是这种开放模型热潮的真正开始 - 我知道 BERT 已经在分类等方面很流行，但 T5 是第一种普遍有用的模型，微调起来非常简单，并且至今仍在使用（t5 基础在 Huggingface 上每月的平均下载量仍然超过一百万次），有大量的变体，并且有点启动了整个社区。 美国实验室受到了很多批评，但谷歌在很多方面都给予了大力支持和开放，推动了整个努力的发展，尽管我觉得近年来他们的开放模型在透明度方面有所下降。完全同意，只能向任何人推荐 T5 作为基础。 无论是作为学习资源还是用于真正的（尽管非常定制的）应用程序，上手都是令人惊奇的。 特别是 BigScience 的微调是一个很好的起点，作为一个外行，我学到了很多东西，特别是关于如何通过各种方法优化模型，因为即使 mt0 也足够小，可以快速连续地进行多次运行，结果截然不同。 量化、修剪词汇、尝试不同的方法来获取训练数据、重新训练数十次，这一切在消费类硬件上都是可能的 [0]，并且令人惊讶的是您可以在功能方面压缩多少。 延迟如何变化与内存使用情况、影响格式可靠性的因素、语言和脚本如何影响训练和效率方程等都是非常值得学习的。了解为什么 T5Gemma 不再在 Apache-2.0 下使用，老实说，在我的实验中测试 T5Gemma 与 T0 相比时，并没有看到太大的优势，但是，仍然有充分的理由说明为什么普通的旧 T5 及其后代仍然流行，许可就是其中之一。Gemma 团队也有非常一致的有趣模型，尤其是像扩散宝石。 讽刺的是，（除了 2.5 Pro 之外），我从来没有热衷于 Gemini 系列型号，但对 Gemma 型号的评价远高于其他型号。 Qwen 直接竞争。 无论如何，感谢这些背后的团队尽可能地做到了这一点。[0]正如在适当的消费级硬件中一样，DGX Sparks 或 Mac Studio 的集群不仅仅用于有时被断言为消费级的实验......他们只是说他们在 Deepmind 从事 Gemma 的工作。 按理说，截至撰写本文时，我们应该假设答案是肯定的。什么？我刚刚开始享受Gemma E4B的发布，你为什么在这里给我洗冷水澡，告诉我可能没有Gemma 5？希望美国最高领导人像习主席那样发表讲话。不要向大公司的工程师询问发布日期，他们要么不知道，要么无权透露。这根本不是真的。 llama 开源的原因很简单，因为它被泄露了，然后 llama.cpp 才是真正的游戏规则改变者，它是在极短的时间内从头开始构建的。 Meta 无奈，只好拿了L，“支持”开源社区。 愤怒的“我恨你，我希望你死”之类的支持。回想起来，很难知道什么是策略，什么是运气。 当时正值歇斯底里地呼吁限制“人工智能研究人员”和安全/道德类型的访问，而非常简单的做法仍然有很大的影响力（我想三年后我们会对当前的《神鬼寓言》内容有同样的感觉）。 Meta 可能很难直接发布它。最终发生的事情是相当有限的门控，然后是“泄漏”的磁力链接和 llama.cpp，这确实带来了开放使用的一场彻底革命，并彻底改变了对话。我不知道 Meta 在这里扮演了什么角色，它可能没什么，但如果他们真的担心泄漏，他们当然可以更加谨慎。 结果是个人和开源人工智能的使用轨迹甚至有关它的对话发生了巨大变化。 无论确切的意图是什么，他们都是关键人物。Meta 将人工智能公司的严重预感视为通过监管捕获来排挤传统公司的一种手段。我不明白你怎么能看待现在正在发生的事情，并称人们只是呼吁谨慎“歇斯底里”不要含糊其辞，但现在正在发生什么？肯定有一些骗局和一些软件缺陷被暴露，但我认为对于技术的革命性飞跃来说，这一切都相当平静。 革命性的技术进步往往会带来一些严重的后果。 例如，直到今天（经过一个世纪的安全改进），汽车每年仍然造成超过一百万人死亡，更不用说破坏大气层了，但这被认为是为了能够更快地在不同地方之间移动而付出的合理代价。我认为汽车是一个很好的例子的原因是，这肯定远远高于我们为法学硕士支付的任何价格，或者可能永远高于，但法学硕士的总体“积极”影响可能远远大于汽车。 必须在引号中加上“积极”，因为自动化等的可能性将是...... 细致入微.... 实际上，但至少从长远来看，这将是一件非常好的事情。> 现在发生了什么？我认为他们指的是法学硕士逃离禁闭并无提示地侵入其他公司系统> 认为这是一个合理的代价这不是一个普遍的观点，也许，就像法学硕士一样，我们应该听取专家的意见，而不是吞噬整个行业强加给我们的一切（为了保持你的汽车比喻：SUV现在在所有欧洲城市无处不在，没有任何逻辑原因应该是这样）这就像，你的意见哥们……我认识的白领中没有一个不担心他们在 llms 的工作。 每一个。 单身的。 一。 我问过律师、医生、任何类型的办公室职员。 白领的定义。 另外，不要让我开始从事各种自动化的蓝领工作，如司机、仓库工人等。我们能得到什么回报？ 更好的搜索（目前，它已经充斥着广告，根据定义，这些广告扭曲了出价最高的人的真理），为一些绝望的人提供了一些值得怀疑的心理治疗师。 还有什么？ 汽车不会飞，哎呀，它们甚至没有以任何可用的方式自动驾驶，我所看到的到处都是社会深陷困境，战争，环境达到糟糕的地方并走向更糟，精神不稳定的人掌握了太多的权力，在早晨的突发奇想中摧毁了数百万人的生活。每个人都觉得这是一场革命，它应该是，它一定是正确的，只要看看数字。 就像众所周知的拿着锤子的人一样，一把非常闪亮、很酷的锤子，正在寻找用它做什么。 我们都看到，在更严厉/资本主义的公司中，反社会的管理是如何寻找任何让员工集体离职的迹象。我可以继续很长一段时间。 对于大多数人来说，讨厌的事情有很多，而值得高兴的事情却很少。 似乎人类有能力从人类身上得到最好和最坏的东西，而最坏的部分似乎是丰富的。 一场革命，即 0.1% 的人会变得更加富有，而其他人则相反，1984 年似乎是现实的温和版本。<< 看来人类有能力从人类身上获得最好和最坏的东西，我想我可以同意这一点。 技术似乎确实有办法让我们最坏的倾向具体化。<<每个人都觉得这是一场革命我对这个类比微笑了，但我要提醒你不要轻视它。 高管们推动这一点是有原因的。 其中有足够的一场革命让事情变得复杂——就好像它还没有发生一样。<<在早上的突发奇想中摧毁了数百万人的生活。确实，但我不太确定在个人层面上可以做些什么。<<我不知道有哪个白领不担心他们在 llms 的工作。不知道。 未来几年可能会好起来。 社会管理者可能无法一口气颠覆一切。 他们会失去太多。 我不能说我完全担心。 我可以看到潜在的影响，但我认为只要我们不将其仅限于总结电子邮件，潜在的好处就是值得的。我要这么说——我认为你只是花了很多时间和非常消极的人在一起，可能是在社交媒体泡沫中。你提到的很多东西并不是真正的人工智能（我同意失业的风险是真实存在的），而只是人类自诞生以来就已经摆脱的日常事物。我认为你不能将当时的讨论简单地描述为呼吁谨慎。 我们曾认真尝试过将所有对甚至是非常基本的法学硕士技术的访问权限都锁定在一个专有的行会中。如果你抓住最极端的例子，你就可以争论任何事情。 普遍的感觉是“谨慎行事”和“我们需要考虑这一点”。哦，停下来，目前的一批LLMS已经够糟糕的了，他们如何削弱这些。 如果“我们需要考虑这个”的人群继续掌权，情况会更糟。 至少现在，我们可以同时拥有：安全的公司垃圾和你想要的任何LLM。您是否知道，如果火车或汽车的时速超过 30 英里，对公众健康来说将是灾难性的？ 不是因为意外。 只是（咳咳）加速造成的创伤：https://illustrationfacts.com/the-train-speed-panic-why-peop...现在歇斯底里仍然存在的原因是，过去和现在，我们正在弄清楚如何处理不仅仅是增量变化的事情。具有讽刺意味的是，道路和人行道应该发生更多变化。 我们从来没有抽出时间来实现零死亡*的良好控制，我们认为每天 100 人死亡是一个合理的便利成本。我们的网络流量和网络行人控制需要改变多少才能让每个人都能驱动人工智能？ 汽车座椅？ 安全带？ 气囊？ 限速器？ 仅限行人居住的空间？ 无人驾驶汽车？许多实际的反应，可能是我们还没有想到的事情的混合体，就像马和马车不需要它们中的大多数共存一样。 控件的发展就像疤痕组织一样，比预先出现的更自然。 **如果对法学硕士的更好类比结果证明它不太像汽车，而更像易燃气体飞艇，我们也会弄清楚这一点，并为几代人讲述警示故事...... 但早在这些故事被遗忘之前，我们就已经想出了一些更实用、更快的东西，而且——哦好吧——也许每英里甚至更致命。---*仍在研究https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vision_Zero**并不是说事情就应该如此。我不同意嘲笑这些事情。 称之为歇斯底里和遭受傲慢之间只有一线之隔。 泰坦尼克号是一个完全相反的歇斯底里的例子。 他们非常自信它能起作用，但它根本不起作用。 所以，是的，仅仅嘲笑愚蠢的人并不能成为消除疑虑的有效论据。另一方面，由于公众和主题专家之间在主题上的分歧，出现了某种歇斯底里症。 有点像邓宁·克鲁格。 以人们说5G会致癌为例。 然后有些人会一概不理会他们的担忧，因为“这不会电离你这个傻瓜”。 只要有足够的功率，您仍然可以用非电离辐射来炸人，例如在无线电广播中。 当然，普通的 5G 天线无法输出这种功率，但我的观点是，人们太快地提出或消除担忧，而没有真正批判性地审视整个主题。 由于各个领域的专业化和进步，这种情况可能会变得更糟，普通人会越来越落后。当你说火车和汽车的时速不能超过 30 英里/小时时，你迷失了我。 哈哈，这听起来像是阿米什人的宣传。 去买你的马和马车又一个冷嘲热讽的受害者。 如果你检查这个链接，很明显他们正在谈论一个所谓的当代关于火车对健康影响的担忧，这意味着今天人们也非理性地害怕科技。问题是我相当确定这个链接过分夸大了它的情况，看起来像一个内容农场。 具有讽刺意味的是，甚至可能是人工智能自身的失误！ 例如，它谈到“铁路脊椎”：“当时的医生认为，火车旅行的不和谐运动和振动可能会破坏神经系统，造成持久的精神和情绪困扰。”这是胡说八道。 作为“文章”可信度低的一个例子，铁路脊柱是火车相撞事故的结果，这是一次明显的创伤性事件，所描述的症状部分只是创伤后应激障碍，一种真实的状况和真正的担忧（不是正常的铁路旅行）。 就这一点而言，当时的铁路旅行确实令人不愉快（大量的振动和刺耳的运动，通风不良的车厢等等），具有讽刺意味的是，现代科学可能会证实这存在某种健康风险。实际上，我认为列出的火车偏执症的例子是历史无知的一个很好的例子。
